title: Sustainable Method for Mitigating Salt Stress in Rice Seedlings
author: Mahmud, Islam, et al.

steps.title: Harvest nodulated legume plants
steps.instruction: Collect legume plants bearing root nodules (yard‑long beans, common beans, shame plants, dhaincha) from Bangladeshi coastal sites with soils ranging from sandy loam to sandy clay loam, pH 7.83–8.10 and organic matter up to 6.22 %.

steps.title: Surface‑sterilize roots
steps.instruction: Rinse the harvested roots gently with tap water, then sterilize them in 0.1 % (w/v) mercuric chloride (HgCl₂) for 5 min, follow with 95 % (v/v) ethanol for 10 s, and finally wash thoroughly with sterile distilled water.

substeps.instruction: Immerse roots in 0.1 % HgCl₂ solution for 5 min.
Immerse roots in 95 % ethanol for 10 s.
Rinse roots with sterile distilled water.

steps.title: Prepare bacterial suspension
steps.instruction: Crush the sterilized roots with a sterilized glass rod in 5 mL sterile distilled water to release bacteria, producing an opaque‑white suspension.

steps.title: Plate bacteria on YEMA agar
steps.instruction: Spread 0.1 mL of the suspension onto an autoclaved YEMA (Yeast Extract Mannitol Agar) plate and incubate for 3–4 days at 29 °C.

substeps.instruction: Apply 0.1 mL suspension to YEMA plate using spread‑plate method.

steps.title: Isolate pure bacterial culture
steps.instruction: Streak colonies from the incubated plate onto fresh YEMA medium to obtain single, pure colonies.

substeps.instruction: Select distinct colonies and streak onto fresh YEMA agar.
Incubate until isolated single colonies are visible.

steps.title: Store culture at –80 °C
steps.instruction: Preserve single colonies from the pure cultures in a –80 °C freezer for future research.
